A 4-year-old Arab boy presented to our clinic with exfoliated maxillary right central and lateral incisor. Gingivitis and plaque accumulation were present in his remaining teeth. The BPE showed a code between 3 and 4 in his remaining teeth. There was alveolar bone destruction around all erupted and erupting dentition. Keratosis of his palms and soles was present at a mild degree (Fig. 2 and Table 1). Scaling was performed in our clinic. We advised that he had periodic oral hygiene measures. A temporary denture was fabricated to wear during the daytime.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Real patient clinical photograph showing bilateral palmar erythema with thick hyperkeratotic scaling, the classic transgredient palmoplantar keratoderma of Papillon-Lefèvre Syndrome, in a disease-focused case report of PLS cutaneous manifestations. The in-text notes failure to thrive and that she walked steadily, indicating a young child; visible skin is light. B: Real patient clinical photograph showing well-demarcated erythematous hyperkeratotic plaques on the extensor surfaces of both knees (ectopic/dorsal keratotic plaques), a recognized cutaneous manifestation of Papillon-Lefèvre Syndrome per the caption and in-text. The article is a PLS case report; the in-text describes a young child (failure to thrive, walked steadily). Visible skin is light. No arrows or diagnostic annotations are present, only the panel label.

in_text_mentions: and shorter than average, consistent with failure to thrive. Despite this, she walked steadily and displayed no signs of cognitive impairment. The skin assessment revealed palmoplantar keratoderma and well-defined, psoriatic-like erythematous keratotic plaques bilaterally affecting her palms, soles, and knees Figure 1 and Figure 2. She had no features of ichthyosis, erythroderma, or generalized scaling. In addition, she had no hair or nail abnormalities. An oral examination found no gingival inflammation, generalized periodontitis, deep pocketing around teeth, hypermobile molars, or halitosis.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Clinical photograph of the palmar surface of a patient from a case report of Papillon-Lefèvre Syndrome showing thickened hyperkeratotic skin with erosions, fissures, and hemorrhagic crusts, consistent with transgredient palmoplantar keratoderma, the hallmark cutaneous manifestation of PLS. The in-text confirms palmoplantar keratoderma affecting palms, soles, and knees in this PLS patient. B: Clinical photograph of the dorsal hand/knuckles of the same PLS patient showing erythematous hyperkeratotic plaques with overlying scale, corresponding to the ectopic (dorsal) keratotic plaques recognized in Papillon-Lefèvre Syndrome. The in-text confirms psoriatic-like erythematous keratotic plaques affecting palms, soles, and knees in this PLS case.

in_text_mentions: and shorter than average, consistent with failure to thrive. Despite this, she walked steadily and displayed no signs of cognitive impairment. The skin assessment revealed palmoplantar keratoderma and well-defined, psoriatic-like erythematous keratotic plaques bilaterally affecting her palms, soles, and knees Figure 1 and Figure 2. She had no features of ichthyosis, erythroderma, or generalized scaling. In addition, she had no hair or nail abnormalities. An oral examination found no gingival inflammation, generalized periodontitis, deep pocketing around teeth, hypermobile molars, or halitosis.
